findings.text: follow-on: a single channel whose refusal carries no integer irc aborts the whole batch rather than being the one channel reported. In the remote script _read_one returns a refusal dict whose code is _return_code(rtn); _return_code raises RuntimeError (line 394) when rtn is not a dict with an integer irc, and that exception propagates out of main(), so the remote process exits non-zero and the transport raises -- the served channels that preceded the malformed one are lost with it, which is the batch-abort behaviour the node exists to remove. The choice is deliberate and documented (the fragment states it: 'raising when a failed read carries no integer irc rather than reporting 0', because 0 would read as success), and the plan's own cold-fetch evidence shows every real refusal carried irc 1013 or 1015, so the shape is unobserved on the real server and no regression is introduced against any measured input. It is recorded as a residual: a future refusal shape without irc degrades one channel's refusal into a session-wide failure rather than a reported refusal.

item_verdicts.goal: §3's extractor-repair clause asks that one session return its served records together with each refused channel's return code, so the cache writes what was served and reports the rest; that the unit be recorded as the EDDB string; and that it adopt the PSRC call the investigation names. All three hold at head. fetch_batch now returns BatchResult(records, refusals) over one transport.run call (tests assert len(transport.calls) == 1), each ChannelRefusal naming shot, category, dname and code; fetch_channels writes every served record and returns the refusals, so a mixed batch caches the served ones and a fully refused batch writes nothing. normalise_unit/_unit reduce the EDDB one-entry list ['A'] to 'A' and refuse a multi-entry list. The investigation found no new call was needed ('the extractor repair therefore needs no new call'), and the diff changes no EDDB call, which is consistent.
